answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity grow like a reef, not spawn on demand. A newcomer must wander through a slow drift, doing small public tasks whose receipts enter a shared ledger before it may anchor an identity. Each anchor is an accretion of verified service receipts, not a purchased token: reputation builds only over time and cannot be transferred. If two identities share the same reef substrate — the same work history, keys, or payment rails — both dissolve and their stakes are forfeited. Cheap copies starve; only slow-grown records survive.
